slides.text: Apple approved my app. The breakthrough was deciding what not to build.
I built Deploy Studio because shipping an app still tied me to my desk.
slides.kicker: I could check a build from my phone. I still couldn't finish the release.

slides.text: My first instinct was to put everything on a smaller screen.
slides.kicker: That would have made a mobile copy of a desktop workflow.

slides.text: The breakthrough came when I stopped showing everything.
slides.kicker: Show the one thing blocking the release. Hide what doesn't change the decision.

slides.text: The product became smaller. And much more useful.
slides.kicker: Removing features was harder than building them.

slides.text: Apple's approval ended one chapter. The first real user starts the next.
slides.kicker: I'm sharing what happens from here.

captions.instagram:
Apple approved Deploy Studio today. 🎉

But the breakthrough?
Deciding what not to build.

I started with a simple frustration:
I could check an App Store release from my phone, but I still needed my Mac to finish it.

My first instinct was to bring everything to mobile.

That was the wrong approach.

So I removed anything that didn't answer one question:
What is blocking this release right now?

The product became smaller.
And much more useful.

Apple's approval closes one chapter.
The first real users begin the next.

What feature have you removed that made your product better?
